What is the Pulaski County Circuit Court?

The Pulaski County Circuit Court is a trial court with general jurisdiction over civil and criminal cases in Pulaski County. It is located in the county seat of Little Rock and serves as the primary trial court for the county. The court has several divisions, including the civil division, criminal division, juvenile division, and probate division.

Procedures of the Pulaski County Circuit Court

Filing a Lawsuit

To file a lawsuit in the Pulaski County Circuit Court, the plaintiff must file a complaint with the court clerk. The complaint must include a statement of the claim and the relief sought. The plaintiff must also pay a filing fee, which varies depending on the type of case.

Service of Process

After the complaint is filed, the defendant must be served with a copy of the complaint and a summons. This can be done by a sheriff, process server, or other authorized person. The defendant then has a certain amount of time to respond to the complaint.

Discovery

Discovery is the process by which each party obtains evidence from the other party before trial. This can include depositions, interrogatories, and requests for the production of documents.

Trial

If the case goes to trial, a jury will be selected and the parties will present their evidence and arguments. The judge will then make a decision based on the evidence presented.
